flow.costPlain: The direct cost of delivering Arm's designs and support — tiny next to revenue, which is why gross margin is 96.5%.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing new processors and platform technology; the GAAP figure includes $129M of share-based pay (paying staff in shares) and $58M of related employer taxes, net of R&D tax incentives. Engineering headcount rose 23% year over year.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling and running the company; the GAAP figure includes $47M of share-based pay and $23M of related employer taxes, and was driven by a bad debt expense, salaries and professional fees, partly offset by lower bonus costs.

follow100Note: License and royalty revenue split the $100 roughly 50/50 — but R&D took $51.65 of it and SG&A another $25.45. Interest, other gains and equity investments added $6.61 back; tax took $2.24. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Arm calls its direct cost 'cost of sales' ($33M); license revenue hit a record $472M.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted, vs $0.10 a year ago; non-GAAP $0.40

oneTimers: Arm recorded a $24M gain from equity investments in the quarter, which it strips out of its non-GAAP results: excluding it (and share-based pay), non-GAAP net income was $419M versus $223M GAAP.
otherDetail: Other items added $62M: $32M of net interest income, a $6M other non-operating gain, and a $24M gain from equity investments. Tax was a $21M bill — an 8.6% effective rate.
pngFooterNote: Record revenue; license deals drove a 39% jump.

segments.name: License and other revenue
segments.note: Fees for licensing Arm chip designs, plus support and related services; up 72% YoY on multiple high-value license agreements as companies made long-term commitments to use Arm technology in future products, plus contributions from backlog.

segments.name: Royalty revenue
segments.note: A cut of every chip shipped with Arm technology inside; up 17% YoY as Armv9 chips — which command higher royalty rates — spread wider, now around 25% of royalty revenue, up from around 20% last quarter. Smartphone royalties rose 50% YoY; automotive and cloud compute grew, while IoT/embedded declined on inventory correction.

takeaways.text: Revenue rose 39% to a record $939M, above the high end of guidance ($875–925M), on record license revenue of $472M (+72%) as companies signed multiple high-value long-term deals, plus royalty revenue of $467M (+17%). The pipeline looks strong too: remaining performance obligations were $2,168M (+29% YoY) and annualized contract value $1,193M (+14% YoY). Arm guided Q2 FY25 revenue of $780–830M and left full-year guidance unchanged at $3,800–4,100M.
takeaways.title: Record revenue, above guidance

takeaways.text: Smartphone royalty revenue rose 50% year over year as premium phones adopted Armv9 chips, which carry higher royalty rates. Armv9 now contributes around 25% of royalty revenue, up from around 20% last quarter. Automotive royalties grew on chips with higher rates in driver assistance and digital cockpits, and cloud compute benefited from early adoption of Armv9 server chips, while IoT/embedded declined on continued inventory correction.
takeaways.title: Armv9 is lifting what Arm earns per chip

takeaways.text: GAAP net income more than doubled to $223M, or $0.21 per share versus $0.10 a year ago, on a 19.4% operating margin — but R&D climbed to $485M on a 23% jump in engineering headcount as Arm invests in Arm Compute Subsystems. Excluding share-based pay and the equity gain, non-GAAP net income was $419M, or $0.40 per share. Free cash flow was -$348M, seasonally the weakest quarter as Arm pays annual bonuses, and a $573M payroll-tax timing benefit from Q4 reversed.
takeaways.title: Profit more than doubled, but R&D is eating most of the gross profit

verdict: Arm's revenue jumped 39% to a record $939M on record license revenue of $472M, and net income more than doubled to $223M as royalty revenue grew 17% on wider Armv9 adoption.
